To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cretaceous coastal-plain deposits of Arctic Alaska are characterized by a temporal change in plant communities from gymnosperm- to angiosperm- dominated vegetation.

the Cretaceous stratal sequence exposed in Kuk River cutbanks is characterized by five successive florules, representing major vegetation changes, that the floral changes reflect climatic change, and that the sequence of florule changes is synchronous with the gymnosperm-to-angiogenesis transition.

1) the Kuk River area in Arctic Alaska contains a complete succession of Cretaceous coastal-plain strata that range in age from Albian to Conianian (late Mesozoic); and 2) the vegetation of the Kuk River coastal plain changed from gymnosperm dominated to angiosperm dominated in late Cenomian-early Turonion time, and that this transition was accompanied by a change from warmer to cooler climates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the stratigraphic sequence of Cretaceous floras in the Kuk River area?
the stratigraphic distribution, paleoecological interpretation, and paleoclimatic implications of Cretaceous floras in the Kuk River area of northern Alaska.
the stratigraphy, paleobotany, and paleoclimate of Cretaceous plant-bearing deposits of the Kuk River system of Arctic Alaska.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Cretaceous floras from the Kuk River area of Arctic Alaska are a record of the vegetation that occupied an Arctic coastal plain during a period of climatic change from warmer to cooler temperatures.
the plant assemblages of the Kuk River area indicate a gradual climatic change from warm temperate to cool temperate conditions in late Mesozoic times.

the plant-bearing Cretaceous stratum of the Kuk River area represent an eastward extension of a coastal plain flora that was originally described from exposures along the Chandler-Colville River in northeastern Alaska.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cretaceous floras from the Kuk River region are similar to those of other high latitude regions of the world.
the Kuk River coastal plain deposits were deposited in a temperate, lowland setting, with a climate that changed gradually from warm temperate to cool temperate during the late Mesozoic.
the Cretaceous vegetation of the Kuk River region was a temperate, mixed forest of gymnosperms and angiosperms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cretaceous vegetation of Alaska was very different from that which exists today.
we can now place the Kuk River floras into a stratigraphic context and use the stratigraphy and fossil plants as proxies for paleoclimate.
the Kuk River coastal plain of Cretaceous Alaska was not a static environment, but rather was a dynamic landscape in which vegetation and climate changed over time.
